newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate soars on peso weakness.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate soars on peso weakness.

text.p: Mexico's overnight Cetes rate closed up a hefty 190 basis points at 24.80 percent on Monday due to the peso weakening substantially against the dollar and expectations of primary rate hikes this week, traders said.
"We have to keep paying high rates to keep investors here and to avoid the dollar being in as much demand as it was today," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso had weakened 10.5 centavos to 7.7800/7.7850 per dollar at midsession.

Expectations of primary rate hikes were fuelled by Banco de Mexico letting the market close with a liquidity shortage of 20 million pesos. The central bank had balanced liquidity flows since August 16.
"The tumbling peso and Banco de Mexico's decision lead us to expect hikes of 125 basis points, or more," a trader said.
Uncertainty led to supply being concentrated in the term market. Rates on 28-day paper gained to highs of 26.50 percent, or substantially above last week's primary rates of 22.74 percent.
Overnight rates on bank paper meanwhile closed up 150 basis points at 26 percent.
Total credit maturities for Tuesday were estimated at 5.065 billion pesos.
